game: PIT @ CIN Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-16 20:15 ET, outdoors, CIN +5.5, total 45.5

script.base: Market script is a moderate Pittsburgh lead, not a blowout: PIT implied 25.5, CIN 20.0. Rodgers mixes a Gainwell/Warren committee (29 carries each in weeks 3/4/6) with Metcalf as the deep WR1 (18 targets, 253 yards, 219 air). Cincinnati, with Browning, is already pass-leaning (Chase 30 targets, Higgins 21 in weeks 4/5/6 vs Brown 27 carries) and as a 5.5-point dog should throw more if it trails, capping Brown's rush day.
script.flip1: PIT is up two scores by halftime and runs the clock. Gainwell/Warren carries rise, Metcalf's target count dies toward the 20- and 32-yard floors, and Browning is forced into a dropback script that still may not produce yards if Pittsburgh's 40% blitz gets home.
script.flip2: Game stays a one-score shootout or Cincinnati hangs around. Both passing games stay live, Metcalf's explosive path is safer, and Brown can grind back to the 40-42 rush range if Cincinnati never abandons the run.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick (nflverse injury report; inactives not yet locked, ~90 minutes pre-kick not in pack). CIN TE Mike Gesicki Out (pectoral) and TE Tanner Hudson Out (concussion): weeks 4-6 they combined for 11 targets and 33 yards, so the pie is small; next man is Noah Fant (prop listed, not in that target log) or a leak to Chase/Higgins/Iosivas/Brown. CIN WR Charlie Jones Questionable (ribs), minor. CIN G Lucas Patrick Questionable (calf): if he sits, Browning pressure up and Brown rush efficiency down. CIN DE Trey Hendrickson Questionable (hip): if he sits, less edge heat on Rodgers, which helps Metcalf's deep clock. PIT WR Calvin Austin III Out (shoulder): 7 targets, 47 yards, 75 air in weeks 3/4/6 come off the field; redistribution favors Metcalf first, then Jonnu Smith (10 targets/47 yards) and D. Washington (8/82/51). PIT S Miles Killebrew Out (knee) and S DeShon Elliott Questionable (resting, not injury): missing safeties help Cincinnati deep shots (Chase 319 air, Higgins 273 air) if Elliott also sits. PIT LB Malik Harrison Questionable (knee): if out, short middle and RB checkdowns get easier.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack (coverage step limited). Infer only from rates: Cincinnati blitzes 21% (mostly base), Pittsburgh blitzes 40% (pressure looks).
matchup.pressure: CIN blitz 21%; PIT EPA/dropback 0.19 vs blitz and 0.08 vs none, so Rodgers is fine with time, which Cincinnati is likely to give him. PIT blitz 40%; CIN EPA/dropback -0.07 vs blitz and -0.26 vs none, so Browning is negative either way and pressure is the live kill for deep Cincinnati yards.
matchup.bleeds: CIN rush defense allows 4.55 YPC and 17 runs of 10+; pass defense allows 7.96 YPA left (82 att), 7.63 middle (41), 8.04 right (80) and 24 passes of 20+ for 214 yards. PIT rush defense allows 4.13 YPC and 16 runs of 10+; pass defense is strong left (4.6 YPA, 75 att) and leaks middle (9.2, 65 att) and right (8.35, 49 att), with 15 passes of 20+.
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Metcalf, the PIT primary target (219 air yards, 14.1 yards per target in weeks 3/4/6), into a CIN secondary that bleeds every zone and barely blitzes. Secondary overlap is Chase (30 targets, 319 air) into PIT's middle/right leak plus a safety absence, but PIT's 40% blitz and 4.6 left-side YPA cut against a deep-air profile. Brown does not attack a bleed: 9 carries times PIT's 4.13 YPC projects about 37 rush yards.

form: Use weeks cited in the pack, not season averages. Metcalf last4 rec yards 20, 32, 126, 95; weeks 3/4/6 sum to 253 so the recent three are 32, 126, 95 (2 of 3 over 83.5, mean 84.3). The 126 is an explosive that inflates the mean; 4-game median is about 63.5. Chase last4 50, 23, 110, 94; weeks 4-6 sum to 227 so recent three are 23, 110, 94 (2 of 3 over 72.5, mean 75.7) with a 23-yard bust. Higgins 21 targets but only 116 yards (15, 32, 22, 62 last4) so air yards are not converting. Brown rush last4 3, 40, 27, 42; weeks 4-6 are 40, 27, 42 (mean 36.3, 3 of 4 under 41.5). Gainwell rush last4 20, 16, 99, 22 and weeks 3/4/6 = 16+99+22=137, so the 99 is a one-game spike and the other games sit on the 20.5 line. Warren's L3 29/99 rush and 8/45 receiving do not reconcile to last4 rush 37, 48, 47, 52 or rush+rec 59, 134, 81, 63; do not treat that gap as an edge. Fant last4 rec 26, 28, 26, 27 is glued to 26.5 and he is absent from the week 4-6 target list.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Metcalf is Pittsburgh's deep WR1 (18 targets, 253 yards, 219 air in weeks 3/4/6, about 84 yards a game) against a Cincinnati secondary allowing about 8 yards per attempt in every zone and 24 explosives, with Austin out and Cincinnati blitzing only 21 percent so Rodgers has time.
edge_players.must_be_true: Rodgers and Metcalf play full snaps, he keeps about 6 targets, the lead stays inside two scores so the passing game is not shelved, and Hendrickson is not a full-go wrecking the deep clock. Austin's absence does not have to be a huge target bump; the matchup is the edge.
edge_players.kills_it: A 14-plus PIT lead by half turns this into the clock-kill script and the 20- or 32-yard floor; or Cincinnati brackets him and the 126-yard explosive does not repeat. Wind is unknown and would also kill it.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Metcalf finished in the 30s because Pittsburgh led by two scores, fed the committee, and the 126-yard game was the fluke the 20- and 32-yard games already warned about; Hendrickson played and the deep ball never got off. Brown cleared 41.5 on one of the chunk runs Pittsburgh allows (16 of 10-plus) in a game that stayed within a score, so Cincinnati never abandoned him, and 40/42 showed the line was a coin flip the whole time. Unknown outdoor weather, a late Patrick or Elliott decision, or Elliott actually playing would have been the checkpoint that should have re-run this before inactives.
slip_story: Do not force these two onto one ticket: a Pittsburgh blowout helps the Brown rush under and kills the Metcalf over. Base script (moderate PIT lead, CIN pass-leaning) can hit both, but they are separate leans, not a 2-leg story slip. The clean single-script stack would have been Brown rush under with a Cincinnati pass-catcher over; Chase was the cousin and failed the red team, so he stays off. No TDs, no second market on either player, no parlay built here. Pass on Fant, Higgins, Gainwell, Warren, Perine.
